source.basis: Operator spec page; structured facts only, no operator prose reproduced.

reading.body:
CyrusOne's NVA9 campus in Sterling, Virginia publishes 38 MW of IT capacity and 700,000 square feet of technical space, and that is the entire published basis for judging it.

The operator does not publish a rack count, an accelerator count, or a power density. Any rack figure derived from 38 MW is an assumption, not a specification. At 40 kW per rack, a common AI training density, 38 MW is roughly 950 racks. At 10 kW per rack it is roughly 3,800. The gap between those two numbers is the whole point: the same published megawatt figure supports very different pictures of how much compute the building holds, and only the operator can close that gap.

No certifications are listed for this campus. That means the spec page does not state whether the site is qualified for federal, financial, or health-data workloads, and it does not state who occupies it. An empty certification field is an absence of information, not a claim about what the campus can host.

Virginia is the largest state on this map by a wide margin, with 376 mapped facilities and 2,563.4 MW of published capacity across 29 facilities that publish a figure. NVA9's 38 MW ranks 16th among those 29, which puts it in the top tier of published Virginia capacity. But most mapped Virginia sites publish no megawatt figure at all, so the state total is a floor rather than a full accounting of what has been built.
